analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: CPI Preview, Asymmetry in Oil, 2027 Consumer Outlook
key_insights: GS expects October core CPI +0.16% m/m vs +0.2% consensus, and headline CPI +0.21% vs +0.3% consensus, with higher food and energy prices lifting headline.
GS expects core CPI of about +0.1% m/m in November and December, as shelter slows and tariff-related price increases shrink.
About 80% probability of a December hike is priced. Core at 0.2% would be constructive for the rally and 0.3% would challenge it.
Supply today is $42bn of 10yr Treasuries after a relatively weak 3yr auction, with $25bn of 30yr supply on Thursday.
Brent fell almost 6% yesterday and the 10yr barely moved. The desk reads rates as more reflexive to AI growth expectations than to energy.
Two-year inflation pricing has rolled over back to summer levels. The desk suggests rate hike expectations may follow.
CL1 is back at $85. Trump's talks with Gulf leaders suggest little appetite for escalation, and regional governments favor economic pressure on Iran over military action.
The desk's oil scenarios are $70-75 if the war ends and $100-110 if it escalates, so the trade is skewed to the upside. Portfolios probably lose money on escalation.
Suggested oil hedge is year-end calls, call spreads or dual binaries. Federal government funding expires December 11.
GS estimates US consumer spending rises 2.5% in 2026 (Q4/Q4) and 2.2% in 2027, near potential. The consumer has been more resilient than expected when the Iran war began and energy prices spiked.
GS expects real income growth to pick up to 2.3% in 2027 as disinflation from tariffs, energy and AI-related prices fades.
GS is not concerned by the measured 3.8% saving rate, which it estimates is closer to 5% after incorporating timelier source data.

GS expects a softer start to 2027 from higher rates weighing on durables, elevated energy prices and lower nonprofit spending after the midterms. A pickup follows as inflation abates and tax refunds and reversal of benefit cuts turn fiscal impulse modestly positive.
